propositions: _build_jira_backend constructs an AcliClient transport without validating that JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, and JIRA_API_TOKEN are present and non-empty, allowing a wholly-unconfigured Cloud environment to build a backend that fails only at first API call with misleading anonymous-access errors.

Cloud adapter lacks the construction-time presence and format guard that DC adapter has for JIRA_PAT, creating a test-parity gap: DC fails loudly at backend construction, Cloud builds silently and fails later.

_build_jira_backend must validate that JIRA_USER contains an email format (non-empty local and domain parts separated by @) before constructing AcliClient, because Cloud authenticates via Atlassian account email as Basic-auth username and a bare handle silently 401s.

The test test_cloud_build_backend_with_missing_credentials_does_not_fail_loudly pins the old silent-build behavior and must be flipped to assert loud BackendEnvError, achieving parity with DC's test_dc_pat_required_heldout.py.

test_the_cloud_factory_also_asserts_conformance uses invalid creds (user='x' not an email) to bypass construction and reach conformance assertions; its fixture must be updated to valid email (user='x@example.com') so the credential guard passes before conformance check.
BackendEnvError raised on missing or invalid credentials must name every missing variable and explain the anonymous-access consequence, mirroring DC's fail-closed message shape.
